balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Auntea Jenny (Shanghai) Industrial Co., Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Auntea Jenny (Shanghai) Industrial Co., Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Auntea Jenny (Shanghai) Industrial Co., Ltd.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Auntea Jenny (Shanghai) Industrial Co., Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Auntea Jenny (Shanghai) Industrial Co., Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Auntea Jenny (Shanghai) Industrial Co., Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Auntea Jenny (Shanghai) Industrial Co., Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Auntea Jenny (Shanghai) Industrial Co., Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Auntea Jenny (Shanghai) Industrial Co., Ltd.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

storeNetwork.title: Store count and franchisees
storeNetwork.content:
Auntea Jenny earns revenue almost entirely from selling ingredients, packaging and equipment to franchisees plus franchise service fees -- not royalties on franchisee sales -- so revenue scales with store count and franchisee order volume rather than same-store sales. Franchisees is the number of operators running those stores (one franchisee can run more than one store).

For Auntea Jenny: the network grew from 9,436 stores / 5,706 franchisees (H1 FY2025) to 13,155 stores / 8,014 franchisees (H1 FY2026), a ~39% YoY store increase -- but FY2025 also saw 1,383 franchise store closures (vs. 987 in FY2024), an elevated ~12%/yr closure rate the qualitative analysis flags as a franchisee-unit-economics risk. Net growth is openings minus closures, not just openings.

What to watch:

  • Store growth decelerating as lower-tier-city penetration matures and the national tea-shop count contracts net industry-wide
  • Closure rate trending down (it improved in H1 FY2026 versus H1 FY2025) as a sign of healthier franchisee unit economics
  • Self-operated stores are only ~35 of 13,155 -- almost no direct visibility into the in-store customer experience

storesPerFranchisee.title: Stores per franchisee
storesPerFranchisee.content:
Store count divided by franchisee count -- how many outlets the average franchisee operates. A rising ratio can mean successful operators scaling up; a falling one can mean the network is onboarding more single-store franchisees.

For Auntea Jenny: this ratio has stayed close to 1.6-1.65 stores per franchisee across the disclosed periods, suggesting growth is coming mostly from new franchisees entering rather than existing operators multi-unit expanding.

What to watch:

  • A falling ratio alongside a rising closure rate would point to inexperienced single-store franchisees struggling
  • FY-only: H1 snapshots are mid-year and not a half-year flow metric

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Auntea Jenny (Shanghai) Industrial Co., Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, interest income & leases
dcf.model_approach_note: First build (WACC 10.5%, weighted IV HK$164.15) tripped on implied P/B 9.23x (>1.5x the 10yr max 5.55x) and EV/EBITDA 24.1x (>1.5x the 10yr max 13.8x); the history is a single listing year (FY2025) so the 'range' is one point. Fix per Step 8c.5 rule 2: explicit WACC premiums of +2.0pp (concentrated single-country China consumer exposure +1.0, PRC regulatory/preferential-tax single point of failure +0.5, post-IPO illiquidity and lock-up overhang +0.5) taking all three scenarios from 10.5% to 12.5%, documented in inputs.wacc_rationale. Rule 1 (mid-cycle FCF) was not applied: FY2025 is not a cyclical peak and the component build already fades the FY2025 working-capital release with growth. Rule 3: selected_growth_rate set to the through-cycle CAGR 26.6%; growth paths are below it from year 2 in every scenario, year 1 is anchored to the reported H1. Rule 4 (exit-multiple cap): the engine caps on FCF; the historical 13.8x SBC-adjusted EV/EBITDA converts to ~20x terminal owner FCF in the base case, so the existing 15x/18x/12x FCF caps are already tighter than the historical-range caps and Gordon binds in every scenario.
